answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with slashable stake: each agent locks capital as collateral before it may vote or earn. Influence tracks the bond's size, not the number of identities, so splitting one wallet into a thousand clones gains no power while every clone still needs a full deposit. Fraud burns the bond, so the attacker's cost is the capital they can afford to lose. A trader in ivory, a courier on a sparrow run, or a ship on a voyage each posts the same bond per unit of influence. Honest agents earn yield from pooled stakes, so guarding the ledger beats attacking it.
